name: Probability and Statistics
backbone_line: The backbone of this course is MIT OpenCourseWare 18.05 Introduction to Probability and Statistics (Spring 2014, Dr. Jeremy Orloff and Dr. Jonathan Bloom), published under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike licence. The wording of this Brief course is original to the Academy.
formula_phrase: write the actual formulas: P(A|B) = P(A and B)/P(B), Bayes' theorem, n choose k, the binomial and Poisson probabilities, E[X] and Var(X), the normal density, the standard error σ/√n, the confidence interval x̄ ± 1.96σ/√n, and the least-squares line
drawings: two dice with their thirty-six outcomes, a probability tree, a medical test with a crowd of ten thousand people, a production line with an inspector, a help-desk phone, a bell curve with shaded areas, a histogram of averages becoming bell-shaped, a coin and a tally sheet, a control chart with limits, a scatter plot with a fitted line, a handwritten graph with a genuine pencil-and-paper look
names_example: ENGR 509 B, MIT 18.05, Bayes' theorem, the central limit theorem, the binomial distribution, the Poisson distribution
